title_en: Supreme People's Court, Supreme People's Procuratorate, Ministry of Public Security, and Ministry of Justice — Standards for Identification of Minor Injuries to the Human Body (Trial Implementation)
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court, Supreme People's Procuratorate, Ministry of Public Security, Ministry of Justice

Standards for Identification of Minor Injuries (Trial Implementation)

Fa (Si) Fa [1990] No. 6

Chapter 1 General Provisions

Article 1 These Standards are formulated in accordance with the relevant provisions of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China, based on the theories and techniques of medicine and forensic medicine, and combined with practical experience in forensic case examination, to provide a basis for the identification of minor injuries.

Article 2 A minor injury refers to an injury that is caused by various external factors, including physical, chemical, and biological factors, acting on the human body, resulting in a certain degree of damage to the structure of tissues or organs, or partial functional impairment, which does not yet constitute a serious injury and is not a slight injury.

Article 3 The assessment of the degree of injury shall be based on the primary damage and consequences directly caused by external factors to the human body, including the condition of the injury at the time of injury, complications and sequelae arising after the injury, and shall be comprehensively analyzed and evaluated.

Article 4 An identifier shall be a forensic physician or a person with forensic medical identification qualifications; it may also be a person at the level of attending physician or above employed or entrusted by judicial organs.
The identifier has the right to understand the case, consult case files, medical records, and inspect the scene, and relevant units have the responsibility to cooperate.
The identifier must adhere to the principle of seeking truth from facts, apply scientific testing methods, maintain case confidentiality, and comply with relevant legal provisions.

Chapter 2 Head and Neck Injuries

Article 5 Subgaleal hematoma.
Scalp avulsion wound area reaching 20 square centimeters (10 square centimeters for children); traumatic scalp defect area reaching 10 square centimeters (5 square centimeters for children).

Article 6 Cumulative length of sharp instrument wounds on the scalp reaching 8 centimeters (6 centimeters for children); cumulative length of blunt instrument wounds reaching 6 centimeters (4 centimeters for children).

Article 7 Simple skull fracture.

Article 8 Head injury confirmed to have caused transient disturbance of consciousness and recent memory loss.

Article 9 Eye injuries:
(1) Eyelid injury affecting appearance or function;
(2) Simple orbital fracture;
(3) Partial lacrimal apparatus injury with functional impairment;
(4) Partial structural injury to the eyeball affecting appearance or function;
(5) Injury leading to decreased visual acuity: corrected visual acuity of both eyes decreased to below 0.7 (a decrease of more than 0.2 compared to pre-injury visual acuity), or corrected visual acuity of one eye decreased to below 0.5 (a decrease of more than 0.3 compared to pre-injury visual acuity); if the original single eye had low vision, the visual acuity decreases by one level after injury. Mild visual field defect;
(6) Traumatic strabismus.

Article 10 Nasal injuries:
(1) Comminuted fracture of the nasal bone, or linear fracture of the nasal bone with obvious displacement;
(2) Nasal injury obviously affecting nasal appearance or function.

Article 11 Ear injuries:
(1) Auricle injury causing obvious deformity; defect of one auricle reaching 10% of one ear, or cumulative defect of both auricles reaching 15% of one ear;
(2) Traumatic perforation of the tympanic membrane;
(3) External auditory canal injury causing stenosis of the external auditory canal;
(4) Ear injury causing hearing loss of 41 decibels in one ear, or 30 decibels in both ears.

Article 12 Oral cavity injuries:
(1) Lip injury affecting appearance, pronunciation, or eating;
(2) Loss or fracture of two or more teeth;
(3) Injury to oral tissues or organs affecting speech, chewing, or swallowing functions;
(4) Salivary gland injury with functional impairment.

Article 13 Zygomatic bone fracture or upper/lower jaw fracture; temporomandibular joint injury causing mouth opening (distance between incisal edges of upper and lower central incisors) less than 3 centimeters.

Article 14 Single wound length of facial soft tissue reaching 3.5 centimeters (3 centimeters for children), or cumulative wound length reaching 5 centimeters (4 centimeters for children), or penetrating wound of the maxillofacial region.

Article 15 Obvious scar left after facial injury, single scar length 3 centimeters or cumulative length 4 centimeters; single scar area 2 square centimeters or cumulative area 3 square centimeters; pigmentation change affecting appearance exceeding 6 square centimeters.

Article 16 Facial nerve injury causing partial facial muscle paralysis affecting appearance and function.

Article 17 Single wound length of neck soft tissue reaching 5 centimeters or cumulative wound length reaching 8 centimeters.
If the above provision is not met but there is motor dysfunction.

Article 18 Neck injury causing signs of asphyxia.

Article 19 Neck injury involving the thyroid gland, larynx, trachea, or esophagus.

Chapter 3 Limb Injuries

Article 20 Soft tissue contusion of the limb occupying more than 6% of the total body surface area.

Article 21 Single wound length of limb skin and subcutaneous tissue reaching 10 centimeters (8 centimeters for children) or cumulative total wound length reaching 15 centimeters (12 centimeters for children); injury involving sensory nerves, blood vessels, or tendons affecting function.

Article 22 Traumatic skin defect requiring skin grafting.

Article 23 Hand injuries:
(1) Comminuted fracture of one phalanx (excluding the distal phalanges of the second to fifth fingers) or linear fracture of two phalanges;
(2) Loss of half a phalanx;
(3) Mild contracture, deformity, limited joint movement, or lateral instability after injury;
(4) Scaphoid fracture, lunate dislocation, or complete metacarpal fracture.

Article 24 Foot injuries:
(1) Fracture of two phalanges of toes;
(2) Loss of one toe phalanx;
(3) Fracture of two metatarsals; fracture of tarsals, talus, or calcaneus; ankle joint fracture or tarsometatarsal joint dislocation. Avulsion fractures are excluded.

Article 25 Fracture of a long bone of a limb; patellar fracture.

Article 26 Dislocation of a major limb joint, partial tear of a joint ligament, meniscus injury, or joint dysfunction caused by scar contracture after limb soft tissue injury.

Chapter 4 Trunk and Perineal Injuries

Article 27 Soft tissue contusion of the trunk shall be assessed by reference to Article 20.

Article 28 Wounds of the trunk shall be assessed by reference to Article 21.

Article 29 Penetrating wound of the trunk without injury to internal organs or major blood vessels or nerves.

Article 30 Chest injury causing pneumothorax, hemothorax, or a relatively large area of simple subcutaneous emphysema, without respiratory distress.

Article 31 Compression of the chest causing signs of asphyxia.

Article 32 Fracture of the scapula, clavicle, or sternum; dislocation of the sternoclavicular or acromioclavicular joint.

Article 33 Rib fracture (excluding a single simple linear rib fracture).

Article 34 Female breast injury causing obvious deformity or partial defect of one breast; injury to the mammary duct of one breast.

Article 35 Closed abdominal injury confirmed as contusion of the stomach, intestines, liver, spleen, or pancreas.

Article 36 Traumatic hematuria (microscopic examination: red blood cells >10 per high-power field) lasting for more than two weeks.

Article 37 Perineal soft tissue contusion reaching 10 square centimeters (proportionally less for children) or hematoma not fully absorbed within two weeks.

Article 38 Penile contusion causing difficulty in urination; partial penile defect or deformity; scrotal avulsion, scrotal hematoma, hematocele; dislocation, torsion, or atrophy of one testis.

Article 39 Wound length on the perineum or scrotum reaching 2 centimeters; penile wound length reaching 1 centimeter.

Article 40 Traumatic anal fissure, anal fistula, or anal stenosis.

Article 41 Vaginal laceration, or injury to the uterus or adnexa.

Article 42 Injury causing inevitable abortion in a pregnant woman.

Article 43 Traumatic spinal fracture or dislocation; traumatic disc herniation; traumatic effect on spinal cord function that recovers within a short period.

Article 44 Pelvic fracture.

Chapter 5 Other Injuries

Article 45 Burns and scalds:
(1) Burn area occupying body surface area:
Superficial second degree 5% or more (3% or more for children);
Deep second degree 2% or more (1% or more for children);
Third degree 0.1% or more.
(2) Second degree or above burns or scalds to the head, hands, or perineum affecting appearance, facial features, or motor function.
(3) Burns or scalds to the respiratory tract.

Article 46 Frostbite shall be assessed by reference to relevant articles of these Standards.

Article 47 Electrical burn accompanied by disturbance of consciousness or generalized convulsions at the time of injury.

Article 48 Injury leaving a foreign body retained in deep soft tissue.

Article 49 Hemorrhage from various injuries presenting pre-shock symptoms and signs.

Article 50 Multiple-site soft tissue contusions shall be assessed by reference to Article 20.

Article 51 Multiple-site soft tissue wounds shall be assessed by reference to Article 21.

Article 52 Other physical, chemical, or biological injuries causing mild damage to the structure of human tissues or organs, or partial functional impairment, shall be assessed by reference to relevant articles of these Standards.

Chapter 6 Supplementary Provisions

Article 53 If multiple injuries individually do not meet these Standards, they cannot be simply added up to constitute a minor injury. However, if three types (or categories) of injuries are each close to the Standards, a comprehensive assessment may be made based on the specific circumstances.

Article 54 Where the data specified in these Standards are preceded by "or more" or "or less," they include the stated number.

Article 55 These Standards apply to the forensic medical identification of injuries to another person's physical health as stipulated in the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China.

Article 56 These Standards shall be implemented on a trial basis from July 1, 1990.
